title: Certification of high-dimensional entanglement in continuous-variable systems
authors: Ida Mishra, Simon Morelli, Klára Baksová, Phila Rembold, Nicolai Friis
abstract: The dimensionality of entanglement in high-dimensional quantum systems is quantified by the Schmidt number, whose large value signals potential advantages for quantum communication and quantum computation. A commonly used approach to practical Schmidt-number detection in finite-dimensional systems is based on the estimation of fidelities to pure states with large entanglement dimensionality or lower bounds to these fidelities. However, for mode-entangled continuous-variable systems, the corresponding measurements are typically difficult to realize. Here, we introduce and assess fidelity bounds for Schmidt-number detection based on practically more accessible measurements of the first and second statistical moments of arbitrary continuous-variable quantum states. We provide analytical formulas that allow evaluating these bounds and test them for families of Gaussian and non-Gaussian states, including two-mode squeezed thermal states and photon-added displaced two-mode squeezed vacuum states. We compare our bounds to other methods for the certification of high-dimensional entanglement based on the same measurements.
summary: This paper develops novel, experimentally accessible methods to certify high-dimensional entanglement in continuous-variable quantum systems. By basing entanglement witnesses on measurable first and second statistical moments, it overcomes the limitations of requiring full state tomography. The results provide quantitative comparisons of these new bounds against established methods using specific squeezed and thermal state examples.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of certifying high-dimensional entanglement in continuous-variable (CV) quantum systems, where direct measurements are often impractical.
main_result: The authors introduce and assess new fidelity bounds for detecting the Schmidt number based only on the first and second statistical moments of the quadrature operators.
method: They derive entanglement witnesses by bounding the trace distance between the unknown state and pure Gaussian states, utilizing the measured first and second moments (characterized by the Covariance Matrix).
model_or_system: The focus is on CV quantum systems, particularly mode-entangled pairs of harmonic oscillator degrees of freedom. The analysis tests the method on Gaussian states like two-mode squeezed thermal states and non-Gaussian states like photon-added displaced squeezed vacuum states.
key_observables: Schmidt number (SN), Fidelity ($F$), First and second statistical moments, Covariance Matrix ($\gamma$), and entanglement witnesses.
important_parameters: Squeezing parameters ($r, s$), inverse temperature ($ eta$), and the dimensionality of the system ($M$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on bounding the trace distance using inequalities derived from the first and second moments, which is advantageous as it avoids full state tomography.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the CV framework using the CM, details the new fidelity-based SN bounds by comparing them to existing methods (EoF, linear witnesses), and finally applies these techniques to calculate and compare results for specific Gaussian and non-Gaussian state families.
why_interesting: This work provides a practical, measurement-efficient theoretical tool for quantifying entanglement in CV systems, which is highly relevant for quantum optics and quantum information processing.
